sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('actually', 'unfortunately', 'of course', 'I’m sorry') to indicate an attitude or viewpoint.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: actually / unfortunately / of course / I’m sorry — turn the speaker’s dial toward personal evaluation

positives: Actually I think we should leave now.
Unfortunately, my team lost the match yesterday.
negatives: I went to the shop yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs and adverb phrases ('near', 'far away', 'upstairs', 'downstairs') to indicate place.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: near / far away / upstairs / downstairs — place the event on the spatial stage
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker positions entities in shared physical space

positives: You can't go far away because your parents won't pay for it.
He went downstairs to find his coat.
negatives: I went to the bank yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of degree adverbs ('a little', 'a bit') with verbs to indicate degree or intensity.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: a little / a bit — small step up from zero on the verb’s intensity dial
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker softens the verb’s force without abandoning it

positives: I can speak English a little now.
Could you move a bit closer, please?
negatives: She went to the cinema yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of adverbs ('maybe', 'perhaps') to indicate degrees of certainty.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: maybe / perhaps — place the statement on the uncertain side of the certainty dial
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker distances from commitment to the proposition

positives: Maybe we can walk there because it's not far from my house.
Perhaps I left it in your living room.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs ('therefore', 'furthermore', 'otherwise') to show a relationship between two clauses or sentences.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: therefore / furthermore / otherwise — wire two clauses with a logical link
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker binds clauses into consequence or addition

positives: You don't like cities with a lot of people, therefore I suggest a small school.
Furthermore, the rent is much cheaper there.
negatives: I went to the park yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of focusing adverbs ('particularly', 'especially') to point to or highlight something.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: particularly / especially — spotlight one element from a presumed set
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker isolates one referent above others

positives: I usually read in my free time, particularly in the evenings.
I love all music, especially jazz.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use adverbs as discourse markers to organise text.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: firstly / secondly / furthermore / moreover — map discourse onto ordered slots
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker arranges the text in linear progression

positives: Firstly, I advise you to visit both schools.
Secondly, consider the long-term effects.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of adverbs to indicate degrees of certainty.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: undoubtedly / undeniably / certainly / definitely / surely — mark the proposition with high confidence
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker owns the claim as settled fact

positives: It was undoubtedly an unforgettable experience.
Television programmes are undeniably a powerful influence.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs ('completely', 'obviously', 'clearly', 'actually', 'luckily', 'honestly') to indicate an attitude or viewpoint.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: completely / obviously / clearly / actually / luckily / honestly — dial the speaker’s stance up or down
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker takes explicit ownership of stance

positives: I am completely sure of my answer.
It's obviously much more fun to go on vacation.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of manner adverbs to modify how something happens.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: seriously / completely / entirely / carefully / properly — wider texture palette for HOW
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker expands the texture vocabulary of the action

positives: She should take his warning seriously.
I read the email carefully before replying.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of stance adverbs (simply, truly, surely, apparently, naturally, surprisingly, inevitably) to indicate an attitude or viewpoint.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: simply / truly / surely / apparently / naturally / surprisingly / inevitably — finer-grained stance markers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker marks nuanced distance from the proposition

positives: Obviously everybody has the right to be on a strike.
We can't truly blame ourselves.
negatives: I went to the bank yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of adverbs and adverb phrases to refer to the timing of an event.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: shortly / immediately / eventually / finally / currently / nowadays — finer temporal pointers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker pins the event on a granular S-anchored line

positives: I look forward to hearing from you shortly.
She has recently moved to a new apartment.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of adverbs with adjectives to express degree or intensity.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: completely / absolutely / extremely / totally / utterly / thoroughly — turn the adjective past every default
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker pushes the adjective to the upper extreme

positives: It deals with the friendship between two completely different men.
It is extremely important to finish on time.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs to indicate degrees of certainty.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: probably / possibly / certainly / definitely / surely / presumably — finer-grained certainty markers
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker calibrates commitment to the proposition

positives: And it will probably be on TV next month!
If I were you I'd certainly choose not to go.
negatives: I went to the bank yesterday.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use adverbs mid clause, to distance the writer from what they are saying.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: allegedly / supposedly / reportedly / presumably — disclaim responsibility for the assertion

positives: He came out from school and supposedly joined the best university in Chile.
The witness reportedly saw the suspect run toward the station.
negatives: I went to the cinema yesterday.
